title: Procedural Record
description:
CoALA procedural memory: how to do something. Learned routines, playbooks, and heuristics.

Deliberate narrowing of CoALA: the paper's procedural memory includes the agent's own code, and the authors flag rewriting it as the riskiest learning modality. This agent stores procedures as DATA that a host reads and chooses to follow — never as executable code, and never applied to itself. Every procedural write is additionally gated behind human approval before it becomes retrievable.

trigger.description: The condition under which this procedure applies. Recall matches a query against this first — a procedure retrieved in the wrong situation is worse than no procedure at all.

preconditions.description: What must already be true before the steps are safe to run. A host that cannot verify a precondition should not run the procedure.

steps.description: Ordered instructions in natural language. Instructions, not code: the host decides how to carry each one out.

tool.description: Suggested tool, if the procedure was learned in a context that had one. Advisory only — the host is not obliged to have it.

on_failure.description: What to do if this step fails, e.g. 'skip', 'abort', or a natural-language fallback.

success_signal.description: How a host knows the procedure worked. Without this the usage counters below are unfalsifiable.

approval.description: The gate. A procedural record is invisible to recall until state is 'approved'. Nothing — not the daemon, not a host, not reflection — may set 'approved' without a human reviewer, and unattended runs may only ever queue candidates as 'pending'.

reviewed_by.description: Identifier of the human who approved or rejected. Must be absent while state is 'pending'.

rationale.description: Why it was approved or rejected. Rejections are kept, not deleted: a rejected candidate that keeps being re-proposed is a signal about the proposer.

usage.description: Whether the learned procedure actually works in practice. A procedure with many invocations and few successes should be revised or retired — this is the feedback loop that keeps procedural memory honest.

supersedes.description: Prior procedure this one replaces. Revision is normal; the old version is marked superseded rather than deleted so a regression can be traced.
